title: Personal Credit Cards: Identifying a Recent Unreversed Late Payment Fee
content:
For a card of Personal Credit Cards that pays by automatic payment, the late payment fee whose ground of reversal is in question is a recent one that still stands on the card. This page defines which fee that is and which due date goes with it.

## Definition

1. **Recency.** Only late payment fees that have been on the card for less than one whole calendar month on the day the matter is handled are looked at.
2. **Still standing.** A fee already taken back does not count. Whether an unreversed fee exists in that recent period is found by counting the late payment fees posted to the card within it and taking away the number of late payment fee reversals posted within the same period. A remainder of one or more means an unreversed late payment fee is present; a remainder of zero means there is none for this purpose.
3. **Due date.** The due date that goes with the fee is the payment due date shown on the card's most recent statement.

## Input, judgement, output

| Recent late payment fees | Recent late payment fee reversals | Unreversed fee present |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | yes |
| 1 | 1 | no |
| 2 | 1 | yes |
| 0 | 0 | no |

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

- The matter is handled on 22 July. A late payment fee posted on 3 July and nothing has reversed it: the fee is recent and unreversed.
- A late payment fee posted on 3 July was reversed on 5 July: the count of fees less reversals is zero, so no unreversed fee is present.
- The only late payment fee on the card posted in April: it lies well over a calendar month before 22 July and is outside the recent period.

With no unreversed late payment fee present, there is nothing on which a reversal ground can be set.
